1.meaning: An exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of every flaw, partner, or imperfection — 'Glory be! / How perfect He is!' It is a noun of glorification used to affirm absolute transcendence and purity.
1.grammar: A verbal noun in the accusative case, marked by the -a ending; it functions as an exclamation typically followed by a noun in the genitive ('Glory be to …'). It conveys the act of declaring someone free of any defect.
1.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide; figuratively to declare free of imperfection

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: Captives or prisoners taken in war; people bound and led away after being seized in battle. It is the plural of asīr, 'a captive.'
3.grammar: A plural noun of the pattern faʿlā, used for groups sharing a condition (here, captivity). The fixed final long vowel -ā does not change for case.

4.meaning: With/by His servant — a male worshipper or bondservant who belongs wholly to his master, here the possessor being the third-person masculine singular 'His'.
4.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with' or 'by' and forces the following noun into the genitive case, shown by the -i vowel on 'ʿabd'. The attached -hi is a possessive pronoun meaning 'his'; its -i form (rather than -hu) is the regular shape that follows a genitive/kasra. So the whole reads 'with his servant'.
4.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, worship, submit as a bondservant

5.meaning: 'By night / during the night / a night' — the noun for nighttime, the dark hours.
5.grammar: A noun in the accusative indefinite, marked by -an (tanwīn). This ending is commonly used adverbially to express the time or circumstance of an action ('by night', 'at night').

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: The place of prostration; a mosque — literally the spot where one bows down (sajda) in worship. With the following 'sacred', it names the Sacred Mosque.
7.grammar: A noun of place on the form mafʿil ('the place where prostration is done'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or as the possessed/qualified noun after another ('… OF the mosque').
7.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

8.meaning: The sacred, inviolable, forbidden; that which is set apart and protected, whose violation is prohibited out of reverence. Describes something hallowed.
8.grammar: An adjective on the form faʿāl ('sacred/forbidden'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case; an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes, so this -i matches a preceding genitive noun ('the … sacred').
8.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — being forbidden, sacred, set apart, inviolable

9.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
9.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

10.meaning: The place of prostration; a mosque — literally the spot where one bows down (sajda) in worship. With the following 'sacred', it names the Sacred Mosque.
10.grammar: A noun of place on the form mafʿil ('the place where prostration is done'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or as the possessed/qualified noun after another ('… OF the mosque').
10.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

11.meaning: The farthest, most remote — a superlative adjective meaning the outermost or most distant in place or degree.
11.grammar: The al- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The word follows the afʿal superlative pattern ('most …'). It ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) which does not change for case, so it stays the same whether subject, object, or possessor — a trait of this superlative form.
11.root: ق-ص-و (q-ṣ-w) — distance, remoteness, the farthest reach

12.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

13.meaning: 'We blessed / we bestowed abundant good and lasting benefit upon.' The verb conveys placing barakah — divinely given abundance, growth, and enduring goodness — into something, making it a source of plentiful, sustained benefit.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb in the associative (Form III, lengthened first vowel: fāʿala) pattern, in the 'we' person. Form III typically directs the action toward an object, and with this stem bārak- it conveys conferring blessing upon something. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers of this completed action ('we blessed / we bestowed abundance'). This verb is typically followed by a phrase naming what or whom the blessing was placed upon.

14.meaning: Around, surrounding, in the vicinity of — the encircling space or area that lies all about something or someone. Combined with an attached 'him', it denotes 'his surroundings / what is around him'.
14.grammar: An adverb of place, 'around', in the accusative with its tell-tale -a ending (ḥawla), here joined to the attached pronoun -hu ('his/him'). The -a ending fits its role as a location word ('round about'), and the suffixed -hu shows possession of the surrounding space.
14.root: ح-و-ل (ḥ-w-l) — to turn, surround, encircle; change

15.meaning: So that We may show him — to cause someone to see or perceive something, expressed as a purpose ('in order that We show him').
15.grammar: The li- prefix expresses purpose ('so that / in order to') and puts the verb into the subjunctive, shown by the final -a on the verb stem. The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). This is a causative (form IV) verb, 'to make see / to show'. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him'.
15.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive; in causative, to show

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: Our signs / verses. The plural of āya — a sign, token, or miraculous proof, and also a verse of revelation — with the attached 'our'.
17.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs / verses') with the possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The sound feminine plural ending -āt shows -i, the case used for the genitive (linked to a following word or after a preposition) and the accusative (object of a verb); attaching -nā ('our') also places it in a possessive relationship. So it means 'signs belonging to Us'.

18.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
18.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

19.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
19.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

20.meaning: "the All-Hearing" — one who hears, perceiving all sounds completely and constantly; used as a divine name it denotes the One whose hearing is perfect and all-encompassing.
20.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, enduring quality ('ever-hearing,' not merely 'hearing once'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

21.meaning: The All-Seeing — one who sees perfectly and completely; as a name of Allah it denotes the One whose sight encompasses all things.
21.grammar: The al- prefix is 'the'. The word is an intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, abiding quality of seeing. The final -u is the nominative ending, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or stands as a predicate/name.

1.meaning: "and We gave / brought" — to give, bring, or grant something to someone.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix is "and." This is a past-tense causative verb meaning "to give/bring (to someone)." The -nā ending marks a first-person plural subject ("we") who completed the action.
1.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to give, bring

2.meaning: Mūsā (Moses), the prophet — a proper name.
2.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is indeclinable — its final long 'ā' does not change to show case — so one and the same form serves whether it acts as subject, object, or follows a preposition.

3.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
3.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'and We made it' or 'and We appointed it' — to make, render, or establish something as such, here with a 'we' doer and an 'it' object.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb with a prefixed 'wa-' ('and'). The '-nā' marks the doer as 'we'; the attached '-hu' is the object 'it/him.' The verb means to make, render, set up, or appoint something into a certain state or role.

5.meaning: Guidance — right direction, the showing of the correct way and the leading along it. The term combines pointing out the path and granting success in following it; more than mere information, it is direction toward what is right.

parts.en: indefinite (tanwin) ending on a shortened final vowel

5.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwin) ending marks indefiniteness — 'a guidance' rather than 'the guidance'. Because the word ends in a weak final letter, its case is not audibly distinguished, so this single form covers more than one grammatical position.

6.meaning: 'For the sons/children of …' — combines the preposition 'for/to' with 'sons/children,' indicating that something belongs or is directed to the descendants of someone.
6.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') attached to 'banū' ('sons/children'). Because 'banū' here is in a construct ('… of …') and follows a preposition, it takes the genitive form 'banī,' shown by the '-ī' ending — the case used after prepositions and in possessive links. This word leads into a following name to mean 'the Children of …'.

7.meaning: 'Israel' — the proper name Israel, the by-name of the prophet Jacob (Yaʿqūb), and by extension his descendants.
7.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is grammatically 'diptote' (it does not take nunation), so it shows a single '-a' ending in places where ordinary nouns would take genitive '-i'; the '-a' here simply marks its case without the usual variation.

8.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
8.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

9.meaning: That you take, that you adopt — a present-tense verb (form VIII) meaning to take for oneself, to choose or adopt something. Addressed to a group ('you all'), and in a form used after particles meaning 'that' or 'to'.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive (form VIII) pattern, 'to take for oneself'. The ta- prefix with the plural ending means 'you all'. The ending is -ū (the final 'n' of -ūna has dropped), which marks the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after particles like 'that', 'to', or 'not'.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
10.root: — (preposition)

11.meaning: Apart from Me / instead of Me / below Me — the word dūn marks something as other than, lesser than, or to the exclusion of a reference point; with the attached 'Me' it means 'taking others rather than, or in place of, Myself.'
11.grammar: A relational noun (functioning much like a preposition) meaning 'apart from / other than,' here in the genitive with the first-person possessive pronoun -ī ('me'). The -ī ending is the attached 'my/me' pronoun; dūn governs a following noun in the genitive, so the whole expresses exclusion or substitution: 'to the exclusion of Me.'
11.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — being lower, nearer, or short of something; hence 'other than / besides'

12.meaning: A trustee, guardian, or disposer of affairs — one to whom matters are committed and who is relied upon to manage and protect them.
12.grammar: A noun on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('one who is relied upon'). The '-an' ending (with tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative case: it commonly signals the object of a verb, or the role/capacity in which something serves ('as a …').
12.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — entrusting, reliance, appointing someone to manage one's affairs

1.meaning: Offspring, progeny, descendants — the children and seed that issue from a person, often spanning later generations.
1.grammar: A collective noun for one's progeny, built on a feminine form ending in tāʾ marbūṭa. The word carries one case vowel here: the accusative -a. That vowel is what makes the tāʾ marbūṭa sound as a full -t-, so the ending is pronounced -ta (dhurriyya- + the accusative -a opening the tāʾ marbūṭa). The accusative is the case a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into that state.
1.root: ذ-ر-ر (dh-r-r) — to scatter, disperse; hence scattered seed/offspring

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

3.meaning: 'We carried / bore / transported' — a past-tense verb meaning to lift and carry a load, to bear someone or something, or to convey it from place to place.
3.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The -nā ending means 'we,' identifying the doers of the carrying. It conveys 'we carried/bore.'

4.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
4.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

5.meaning: Noah — the proper name of the Prophet Nūḥ.
5.grammar: A proper name. The -in ending (nunation) shows it is treated as a fully declinable noun in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or to link to a preceding word. (Most personal names are partly indeclinable, but this short name takes full case endings.)

6.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
6.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

7.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

7.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

8.meaning: 'A servant / slave / bondsman' — a human being as one who serves and is wholly owned by, and submissive to, his master. In Qur'anic usage it especially conveys a worshipping servant of Allah.
8.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -an is accusative and indefinite, the case that typically marks the object of a verb or a complement; the final -n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a servant').

9.meaning: Deeply grateful, thankful — an intensive describing one whose thankfulness is abundant and habitual; of a servant, much-thanking, and of a Lord, abundantly rewarding of thanks.
9.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿūl pattern, signalling a quality present in a high or repeated degree. The final -an (with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending: it marks the word as 'a … (something)' and in the state a noun takes as an object or predicate.

1.meaning: 'And We decreed / determined / made known' — a connector plus a past-tense verb meaning to settle, decide, or bring a matter to completion, spoken by a 'we'.
1.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb preceded by 'wa-' ('and'). The suffix '-nā' marks 'we' as the doer. The verb conveys decisively settling or finishing a matter, hence 'and we decreed/determined'.
1.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decree, decide, settle, complete

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
2.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

3.meaning: Sons of / children of — the plural 'sons' used in a possessive construction meaning 'the descendants or people of' someone.
3.grammar: This is the plural of 'son' in the construct (possessive) state, so it leans on a following name meaning 'the children OF …'. The -ī ending here reflects the construct form (the normal final nūn of the plural drops off when the word is joined to what follows), and it carries an oblique (accusative/genitive) sense rather than a nominative one.

4.meaning: 'Israel' — a proper name. In Qur'anic usage it is the by-name of the Prophet Jacob, his descendants being 'the Children of Israel.' As a foreign proper name it carries no Arabic root meaning.
4.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. Being both a proper name and foreign, it is a diptote — taking only two case-shapes and no nunation — so its ending is -a in object/oblique positions rather than -i. The final -a here simply marks it as a governed word (e.g. linked to a preceding noun, or object of a preposition/verb) and carries no independent meaning.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
6.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

7.meaning: You will most surely spread corruption — to ruin, to work moral or social decay and disorder, stated with heavy emphasis that it will certainly happen.
7.grammar: The la- prefix is an oath-like emphasiser ('surely'). The tu- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'). This is a causative (form IV) verb, 'to cause corruption'. The doubled -nna is the heavy emphatic ending that attaches to a verb to stress that the action will certainly take place.

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

10.meaning: Two times, twice — exactly two occurrences of something. It is the dual ('exactly two') form of the noun meaning 'a time/instance'.
10.grammar: A dual noun, meaning 'exactly two' of the thing. The -ayni ending marks the dual in the accusative or genitive state; for an adverb of frequency this conveys 'two times / twice'. Arabic has a special dual distinct from the plural (three or more).
10.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass by; a passing, hence an instance/time

11.meaning: And you will most surely rise high / become overbearing — to be lofty, to exalt oneself or tower over others, stated with strong emphasis.
11.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and'. The la- prefix adds oath-like emphasis ('surely'). The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'). The doubled -nna is the heavy emphatic ending fixed to the verb to stress certainty of the action.
11.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — height, loftiness, rising above

12.meaning: Loftiness, exaltation — being high or elevated; when applied to conduct it means arrogance, overbearing pride, or tyrannical superiority.
12.grammar: A verbal noun (the abstract 'act/state' noun) of rising high. The final -an (with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, marking the word as an object or as an adverbial/specifying complement.
12.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — height, loftiness, rising above

13.meaning: Large, great, big, or major — an adjective describing something of great size, amount, or importance. It can also mean elder/older in age. The -an ending leaves it indefinite ('a large …').
13.grammar: An indefinite adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn): it commonly marks the object of a verb, or works adverbially, and signals the word is indefinite ('a large one'). It pairs with ṣaghīr ('small').
13.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, largeness, being great or old

1.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
1.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

2.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

3.meaning: The promise, pledge, or appointed assurance; a binding undertaking that something will come to pass — whether a good thing promised or a threatened outcome.
3.grammar: A verbal noun, 'a promise/pledge.' The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject; in a possessive phrase it also carries the 'X of Y' sense ('the promise of …'), the following noun completing it.
3.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — promising, pledging, an appointed assurance

4.meaning: The first of the two of them (feminine) — 'the first one' of a pair, with the pair being two feminine or grammatically-feminine things.
4.grammar: 'Ūlā' is the feminine form of 'first'; it ends in a fixed long -ā written with alif maqṣūra (the terminal letter ى spelling that vowel, not a detachable suffix). The attached -humā is a dual possessive pronoun meaning 'of the two of them', referring to two parties. Because 'ūlā' ends in a fixed long -ā, its case does not change in form; the whole means 'the first of the two of them'.

5.meaning: We sent/raised up — to dispatch or commission someone (especially to send a messenger); the root also carries the sense of stirring up or raising to life.
5.grammar: Past-tense verb. The attached -nā ending means 'we' and marks a completed past action ('we sent'). The ending is the subject-marker for a first-person plural that has acted.
5.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to send forth, dispatch, raise up, resurrect

6.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
6.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

7.meaning: Servants or worshippers — human beings considered in their relationship of devotion and submission to Allah. The plural noun stresses dependence on and service to the Lord. It carries an indefinite sense: 'servants', 'some servants'.
7.grammar: This is a plural noun. The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending: it marks the word as indefinite ('servants', not 'the servants') and typically as the object of a verb or otherwise governed in the accusative case.

8.meaning: 'For us / to us' — indicating that something is directed toward, or belongs to, the speaker's group.
8.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). When this pronoun is added, the preposition's vowel becomes 'la-'. The whole expresses benefit or direction toward 'us' — what is done for, or owed to, the speaker's group.
8.root: — (li- is a particle/preposition; -nā is a pronoun)

9.meaning: Possessors of / those endowed with. A word meaning 'owners of' or 'people having' some quality, used to attribute a trait or rank to a group.
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'possessors/people of', which has no singular from its own letters (its singular is supplied by another word). The 'ī' ending here reflects its non-nominative (genitive/accusative) form and it is always followed by a noun naming what is possessed ('possessors OF …').

10.meaning: Might, force, valour in war — formidable strength and the harm or violence it can inflict; also hardship or adversity.
10.grammar: A noun denoting forceful power or distress. The final -in (with tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending: a noun takes this state after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun as 'a … of …'.
10.root: ب-أ-س (b-ʾ-s) — force, might; hardship, adversity

11.meaning: An adjective meaning 'strong, mighty, intense, severe, firm' — describing something powerful and hard to overcome.
11.grammar: Singular indefinite adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The '-in' ending marks it indefinite and genitive, agreeing with an indefinite genitive noun it describes ('a strong …').
11.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, firm, severe

12.meaning: Then they went roving through / penetrated about — to move to and fro searching through a place, ranging back and forth amid it.
12.grammar: The fa- prefix means 'then' or 'so', linking to what precedes. The verb is past tense. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject acting in the past ('they … ed'); the silent alif written after it is a spelling convention.
12.root: ج-و-س (j-w-s) — to go to and fro, roam/search through

13.meaning: Through the midst of / amid — the space, gaps, or inner reaches between and within things.
13.grammar: An adverb-like noun meaning 'amid / through the midst of', typically followed by another noun in the genitive ('through the midst OF …'). The final -a is the accusative ending, the form it takes in this adverbial role.
13.root: خ-ل-ل (kh-l-l) — gap, interval, the space between things

14.meaning: The dwellings, homes, abodes — the houses and the lands or quarters where people live.
14.grammar: The al- prefix is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'd' sound). 'Diyār' is the plural of dār, 'a dwelling/abode'. The final -i is the genitive ending, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun as 'of …'.
14.root: د-و-ر (d-w-r) — to turn/encircle; a dwelling one revolves around

15.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence

16.meaning: A promise / a pledge — a binding commitment to do something, here in the sense of a solemn assurance given.
16.grammar: A masculine singular verbal noun, indefinite and in the accusative case, shown by the '-an' ending (nunation written over an alif). The accusative often marks a direct object or, as with such verbal nouns, an emphatic confirmation ('… as a promise / a sure promise').

17.meaning: Done, carried out, accomplished — a thing that has been acted upon and brought into effect; a settled, fulfilled matter.
17.grammar: A passive participle on the mafʿūl pattern, naming the receiver of an action ('that which is done'). The final -an (with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, the state a noun/adjective takes as an object or predicate-complement.
17.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, to act, to carry out

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: We gave back / returned / repelled — to turn something back, restore it, or drive it away; first-person plural in the past.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The attached -nā is the first-person plural subject ending on a past verb, meaning 'we' did the action ('we gave back / returned').
2.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, give back, repel, restore

3.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
3.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

4.meaning: The turn, the renewed attack, the comeback — a return to a former state or position, often a counter-charge or a fresh round in one's favour.
4.grammar: The al- prefix is 'the'. The noun on the faʿla pattern denotes a single instance of returning or charging, and it ends in a feminine tāʾ marbūṭa. The word carries one case vowel here: the accusative -a, which opens the tāʾ marbūṭa so the ending sounds as a full -ta (al-karra- + the accusative -a). The accusative is the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb.
4.root: ك-ر-ر (k-r-r) — to return, repeat, charge back

5.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
5.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
5.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: And We supplied/reinforced you — to extend aid, supply, or reinforcement to someone; first-person plural past, addressed to a plural 'you'.
6.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and'. This is a causative (form IV) verb, 'to supply / reinforce / extend aid'. The -nā ending marks a first-person plural past subject ('we'), and the attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you' addressed to a group.
6.root: م-د-د (m-d-d) — to extend, stretch, supply, reinforce

7.meaning: With wealth, possessions, property — material goods and riches that a person owns.
7.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with' and forces the following noun into the genitive case. 'Amwāl' is the plural of māl, 'wealth/property'. The final -in (with tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending, the form taken after a preposition while remaining indefinite ('with some wealth').

8.meaning: And sons / children — male offspring (and by extension descendants).
8.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and'. 'Banīn' is a sound masculine plural of ibn, 'son'. In this plural type the nominative (subject) form is -ūna (banūna), while the accusative and genitive form is -īna; the shown -īn(a) ending is therefore the object/genitive form, used when the noun is an object or is linked after a preposition.
8.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — to build; son (one who continues/builds a line)

9.meaning: And We made/appointed you — to make, render, or appoint something into a certain state; first-person plural past, addressed to a plural 'you'.
9.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and'. The verb is past tense, 'to make/render/appoint'. The -nā ending marks a first-person plural past subject ('we'), and the attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you' addressed to a group.
9.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

10.meaning: 'More' / 'greater (in number or amount)' — the comparative/superlative form built from 'much, many', meaning more numerous or more abundant.
10.grammar: A comparative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('more …'). The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is an object or otherwise governed; this pattern does not take nunation. It is typically completed by 'than …'.
10.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much/many, abundance

11.meaning: A band of supporters, fighting force, numbers — the company of men (kin and followers) who rally to one's side and on whom one relies.
11.grammar: A noun on the faʿīl pattern denoting a group that rallies or goes forth together. The final -an (with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, the state a noun takes as an object or as a specifying complement.
11.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — to go forth/rally; a troop that sets out

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: You did good / acted well / excelled — to do what is good and beautiful, to act with excellence and kindness; second-person plural past.
2.grammar: A causative (form IV) verb meaning 'to do good / act excellently'. The attached -tum is the second-person masculine plural subject ending on a past verb, meaning a group 'you' performed the action ('you did good').

3.meaning: You did good / acted well / excelled — to do what is good and beautiful, to act with excellence and kindness; second-person plural past.
3.grammar: A causative (form IV) verb meaning 'to do good / act excellently'. The attached -tum is the second-person masculine plural subject ending on a past verb, meaning a group 'you' performed the action ('you did good').

4.meaning: For yourselves — to or for your own selves/souls; 'nafs' is the self, soul, or person of someone.
4.grammar: The prefix li- means 'for / to' and forces the following noun into the genitive case, shown by the -i vowel. 'Anfus' is the plural of nafs, 'self/soul'. The attached -kum is the possessive pronoun 'your', addressed to a group, giving 'for your own selves'.
4.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person, inner being

5.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
5.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) did evil / acted badly'. It expresses that a group committed wrongdoing, harm, or misdeeds — the opposite of doing good (iḥsān). The sense covers behaving badly toward oneself or others.
6.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached -tum ending marks the doer as 'you all' (second-person masculine plural): a group of people being addressed performed the action. Being past tense, it presents the deed as already done.

7.meaning: Then for her — links a result ('then/so') with 'belonging to / for her', referring to a single female.
7.grammar: A cluster of particles plus a pronoun: fa- ('then/so', marking a consequence), the preposition li- ('for/to', shortened to la- before a pronoun), and the attached pronoun -hā ('her', feminine singular). Altogether: 'then for her'.

8.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
8.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

9.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

10.meaning: The promise, pledge, or appointed assurance; a binding undertaking that something will come to pass — whether a good thing promised or a threatened outcome.
10.grammar: A verbal noun, 'a promise/pledge.' The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject; in a possessive phrase it also carries the 'X of Y' sense ('the promise of …'), the following noun completing it.
10.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — promising, pledging, an appointed assurance

11.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
11.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
11.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'so that the two of them may grieve / distress / bring sorrow to (someone)'. It conveys causing harm, sadness, or disfigurement — making a person's face fall in dismay or inflicting injury that grieves them. The form refers to exactly two doers.
12.grammar: The prefix li- means 'in order to / so that', expressing purpose, and it puts the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (a dependent 'that'-clause), which is why the verb's normally final -ni is dropped, leaving the -ā ending that marks 'they two' (masculine dual) as the doers — exactly two, not a group.
12.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, harm, distress

13.meaning: Faces belonging to a plural 'you' — the front of the heads, the part one turns and directs toward something; can also figuratively mean attention, orientation, or one's whole self as turned somewhere.
13.grammar: A plural noun (singular wajh, 'face') carrying the attached pronoun -kum, 'your' for a group. The -a ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. what is turned or directed).
13.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, to turn toward

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'and so that they may enter / go into'. It denotes entering a place, going inside, or penetrating into something.
14.grammar: Opens with 'and' (wa-), then li- 'so that / in order to' expressing purpose, which places the present-tense verb in the subjunctive mood (a 'that'-clause); the normally final -na is therefore dropped, leaving -ū to mark 'they (masculine plural)' as the doers.
14.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — entering, going in

15.meaning: A place of prostration; a mosque — the building or site where the act of bowing down in worship (sujūd) is performed.
15.grammar: A noun of place built on the pattern maf'il, naming the location where an action happens — here 'the place of prostration.' The definite article al- marks it as 'the.' The -a ending is accusative (object case): it typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
15.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow down

16.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
16.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

17.meaning: A verb meaning 'they entered it'. It states that a group went into something or some place, with 'it' being the thing entered.
17.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The -ū (written with wāw) marks 'they (masculine plural)' as the doers, and the attached -hu is a third-person masculine singular object pronoun ('it/him') — the thing or place they went into. Past tense presents the entering as already accomplished.

18.meaning: First, foremost — the one that comes before all others in time, order, or rank.
18.grammar: A noun/adjective meaning 'first', here in a form that does not take normal indefinite case-tanwīn (a 'diptote'). The -a ending is accusative, marking it as an object or, very often, as the leading term of a possessive phrase ('the first of …').
18.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to return to a beginning

19.meaning: One time / once / an instance — a noun denoting a single occurrence of an act. Indefinite ('a time'), as shown by its two-vowel (tanwin) ending.
19.grammar: A feminine noun meaning 'a single time/occurrence'. The doubled-vowel ending (tanwin, here -in) marks it as indefinite ('a time', not 'the time'); the -i quality of that ending is genitive, signalling the word follows a preposition or links to another noun. It often expresses 'one time / once'.
19.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — passing by; an instance or occurrence of something

20.meaning: A verb meaning 'and so that they may destroy / ruin utterly'. The doubled middle consonant gives an intensive force: to wreck completely, lay waste, or bring to total ruin.
20.grammar: Begins with 'and' (wa-), then li- 'so that / in order to' marking purpose, which puts the present-tense verb in the subjunctive mood; the final -na is dropped, leaving -ū for 'they (masculine plural)'. The doubled middle root letter (form II) intensifies the action — destroying thoroughly, not merely damaging.

21.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
21.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

22.meaning: A verb meaning 'they rose high / became lofty / exalted themselves'. It can describe literally rising or, figuratively, becoming arrogant, gaining the upper hand, or overpowering others through haughty dominance.
22.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The -aw ending marks 'they (masculine plural)' as the doers (this is how the plural ending appears on verbs whose final root letter is a weak/vowel-like letter). Past tense frames the rising or self-exaltation as already done.

23.meaning: A noun meaning 'utter destruction / a ruining / a laying waste'. It is a verbal noun naming the act of destroying completely, often used to reinforce the verb of the same root for emphasis.
23.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action of destroying). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a destruction'); on a verbal noun like this it commonly functions as an emphatic object reinforcing a verb of the same root — 'to destroy with a [thorough] destroying'.

1.meaning: A particle/verb of expectation meaning 'perhaps, it may be that, hopefully'; it introduces something hoped or expected to happen, and when used of Allah it conveys a sure promise.
1.grammar: An invariable verb-like particle expressing hope or expectation ('perhaps, it may be that'). It does not take the usual case or tense endings and typically opens a clause about what is hoped to occur.
1.root: ع-س-ي (ʿ-s-y) — to be hoped for, be likely

2.meaning: Your (plural) Lord — 'Rabb' means the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings a thing to its completion. It combines lordship with loving upbringing and care.
2.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The suffix '-kum' means 'your' (plural possessor). The '-u' on 'rabbu' before the suffix is the nominative case, marking the word as a subject or as a predicate standing on its own.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, own

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'may He have mercy on you (plural) / He shows you mercy'. It expresses Allah bestowing compassion, forgiveness, and tender care upon a group of people.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking 'he' as the doer. The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you (masculine plural)' — the recipients of the mercy. The final -a vowel here reflects the subjunctive/jussive form often carried in conditional and prayer-like constructions ('may He have mercy').

5.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
5.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) returned / went back / reverted'. It denotes coming back to a former state or action, repeating or resuming what was done before.
6.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The -tum ending marks the doers as 'you all' (second-person masculine plural). Past tense presents the returning as already done — often, in such forms, as the condition 'if you go back (to doing something)'.

7.meaning: 'We returned, went back, reverted.' The root means to come back, to return to a place or to a former state, way, or practice. The subject is 'we.'
7.grammar: A past-tense verb (a hollow root whose middle weak letter contracts in this form). The suffix -nā marks the subject 'we' ('we returned / went back').
7.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, come back, revert

8.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We made / appointed / rendered.' This very common verb can mean to create or place something, or to assign something a state or role (to make X into Y).
8.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers. The verb often takes two objects, meaning 'to make/turn one thing into another.'
8.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

9.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
9.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
9.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

10.meaning: A three-part word: 'for' + 'the' + 'those who cover up the truth / reject faith.' The base noun denotes the kāfir — one who disbelieves, denies, and ungratefully conceals the truth and Allah's favor. With 'for,' it marks them as the ones for whom something is intended.
10.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a definite plural noun, masculine. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, here required because it follows the preposition 'li-'. The whole denotes 'for the disbelievers.'
10.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

11.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'a confining bed / a prison / an enclosing mat'. It carries the sense of something woven and spread out that hems one in — a mat or bedding — and by extension a place of confinement that surrounds and restrains.
11.grammar: A noun in the intensive/adjectival pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a confining bed'), the case typically used for the object of a verb or the complement that completes a statement of 'making X into Y'.
11.root: ح-ص-ر (ḥ-ṣ-r) — confining, enclosing, restricting

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

3.meaning: The Qur'an — the recited Scripture; literally 'the Recitation' or 'the Reading'.
3.grammar: A definite noun (carrying 'al-', 'the') on the verbal-noun pattern fuʿlān, denoting the act/thing of reciting. The final '-a' marks the accusative case, which most often signals that the word is the direct object of a verb.
3.root: ق-ر-ء (q-r-ʾ) — reciting, reading aloud, gathering words together

4.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
4.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

5.meaning: A relative expression meaning 'to the one (feminine) which / that' — combining 'for/to' with a feminine relative pronoun pointing to a thing or way that is then described by a following clause.

parts.en: the one which / that (feminine singular relative pronoun)

5.grammar: The prefix li- means 'to / for' (it normally calls for the genitive). It is joined to allatī, the feminine-singular relative pronoun 'the one which / that', which introduces a following clause describing a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.

6.meaning: A standalone pronoun meaning 'she' or 'it' (feminine). Arabic has no neuter, so 'it' for a feminine noun is expressed with this word. Used independently for emphasis or to stand as the subject of a sentence.
6.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person feminine singular. It stands on its own (not attached to another word) and most often functions as the subject of a nominal sentence ('she/it is …'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

7.meaning: An adjective meaning 'most upright / straightest / most sound'. It is the superlative/comparative of 'straight, upright', describing what is most correct, most firmly established, or most just and true.

parts.en: upright / straight / sound (from the 'standing straight' root)

7.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the 'afʿal pattern ('most/more ___'). The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate that describes the subject ('… is most upright').

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'and he gives good news / glad tidings'. The doubled middle consonant gives intensive force: to announce joyful news that visibly gladdens a person (literally, brightens the face/skin).

parts.en: he gives glad tidings (intensive present-tense verb)

8.grammar: Opens with 'and' (wa-). A present-tense verb with the yu- prefix marking 'he' as the doer; the doubled middle root letter (form II) intensifies it into 'announcing good news'. The final -u is the indicative ending, used for a plain ongoing or habitual statement ('he gives / keeps giving glad tidings').
8.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, glad tidings; skin/face brightening with joy

9.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
9.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

10.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
10.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

11.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
11.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
11.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

12.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
12.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
12.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

13.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
13.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

14.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
14.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

15.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
15.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
15.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

16.meaning: Large, great, big, or major — an adjective describing something of great size, amount, or importance. It can also mean elder/older in age. The -an ending leaves it indefinite ('a large …').
16.grammar: An indefinite adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn): it commonly marks the object of a verb, or works adverbially, and signals the word is indefinite ('a large one'). It pairs with ṣaghīr ('small').
16.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, largeness, being great or old

1.meaning: 'And that …' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle anna, which introduces and emphasizes a statement, asserting a fact emphatically (roughly 'and indeed that …'), and grammatically governs the noun that follows it.
1.grammar: A conjunction wa ('and') prefixed to anna, an emphatic particle meaning 'that' (asserting a fact). Anna puts the following noun into the accusative case and typically links a clause to a preceding verb of saying, knowing, or perceiving.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
4.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

5.meaning: The noun 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come,' linked by 'with / for / in exchange for' (bi-). The base word means 'the last, the latter, the final' (state of affairs) and is used as the standing name for the everlasting life after this world.
5.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the Hereafter') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('with / for / in exchange for'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case a noun takes after a preposition (or when linked to a preceding noun as '…of…'). Here it appears because the preposition 'bi-' requires the genitive form; the tā' marbūṭa of the stem is sounded as 't' before this ending.
5.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

6.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we made ready / we prepared in advance,' conveying the deliberate arranging or setting-up of something beforehand so that it stands ready.

parts.en: (part of the stem; the verb is from the form-IV pattern aʿtada)

6.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action verb. The attached -nā ending is the 'we' subject marker, telling you the doers are first-person plural. As a past-tense form it presents the action as already finished and accomplished.

7.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
7.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

8.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
8.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

9.meaning: An adjective meaning 'painful / agonizing'. It describes something that causes intense pain or suffering, whether physical or anguishing.
9.grammar: An adjective in the intensive faʿīl pattern ('intensely ___'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a painful [one]'), the case typically taken by a noun/adjective serving as an object or agreeing with one.

1.meaning: A verb meaning 'and he calls / supplicates / invokes'. It denotes calling upon someone, praying, or asking — often appealing to Allah, but also calling for a thing whether good or ill.
1.grammar: Begins with 'and' (wa-). A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking 'he' as the doer. Its root ends in a weak letter, so the final long vowel is shortened/dropped in this form, leaving 'yadʿu' — a plain statement that 'he calls / prays'.

2.meaning: 'Mankind, the human being, humanity' — the human as a species or as the representative human creature.
2.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') here generalises to the whole class ('humankind as such'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the subject (the doer or the thing spoken about) of a sentence.
2.root: ا-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humankind

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with / for evil / harm'. It joins the preposition 'with, for' to the noun 'evil', denoting something bad, harmful, or malicious — the opposite of good (khayr).
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with / for / by') governs the following noun, which carries the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition like bi-; here it links 'with/for' to 'the evil'.

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'his calling / his supplication / his prayer'. It names the act of invoking or asking, attributed to a single male — 'the prayer that he makes'.
4.grammar: A verbal noun ('the act of calling/praying'). The -a ending is accusative, the case typically taken by the object of a verb or by a noun used in comparison; the attached -hu is the possessive 'his', so it reads 'his supplication / his prayer'.

5.meaning: with, or in regard to, the good — that which is beneficial, wholesome, and desirable.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with / in / for') attached to a noun carrying the definite article al- ('the'). The preposition puts the noun in the genitive, which is the -i ending. The noun denotes goodness or benefit, and can also mean 'better / best'.

6.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

7.meaning: 'Mankind, the human being, humanity' — the human as a species or as the representative human creature.
7.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') here generalises to the whole class ('humankind as such'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the subject (the doer or the thing spoken about) of a sentence.
7.root: ا-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humankind

8.meaning: An adjective meaning 'very hasty / impatient / over-quick'. The intensive pattern stresses an ingrained tendency to rush — wanting things immediately rather than awaiting their proper time.
8.grammar: An adjective in the intensive faʿūl pattern, stressing a deep-seated trait ('habitually hasty'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the case typically used for a predicate completing a statement like '… was/is [ever] hasty' or for an object.

1.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We made / appointed / rendered.' This very common verb can mean to create or place something, or to assign something a state or role (to make X into Y).
1.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers. The verb often takes two objects, meaning 'to make/turn one thing into another.'
1.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

2.meaning: The night — al-layl is the period of darkness from sunset to dawn; the dark portion of the day-night cycle, a time of covering, rest and stillness.
2.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the ending typically given to the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or used adverbially for time ('the night').

3.meaning: And the daytime — the period of daylight between dawn and sunset, the bright span of the day as opposed to night.
3.grammar: A masculine noun with the prefix wa- ('and') and the definite article (here assimilated as n-nahār). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the object of a verb or the thing being pointed to.

4.meaning: A noun meaning 'two signs / two tokens'. A 'sign' (āyah) is a mark, indication, or miraculous token that points to a deeper truth; this is its dual form, meaning exactly two of them.
4.grammar: A dual noun meaning 'two signs'. The -ayni ending marks the dual (exactly two) in its oblique form — the form used for the object of a verb or after a preposition (as opposed to the subject form -āni).

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'then We erased / blotted out / effaced'. It denotes wiping something away so it no longer shows — removing or obliterating a mark, trace, or light.
5.grammar: Opens with fa- ('then / so'), marking a consequence or sequence. A completed (past-tense) verb whose -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers — a plural or majestic 'We'. Past tense presents the erasing as already accomplished.

6.meaning: 'A sign / token / mark' — āyah is a sign that points to something beyond itself; it also denotes a miraculous proof and a verse of revelation.
6.grammar: A singular noun. The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing pointed to or presented), or stands as the predicate of certain particles.

7.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
7.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').

8.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We made / appointed / rendered.' This very common verb can mean to create or place something, or to assign something a state or role (to make X into Y).
8.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers. The verb often takes two objects, meaning 'to make/turn one thing into another.'
8.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

9.meaning: 'A sign / token / mark' — āyah is a sign that points to something beyond itself; it also denotes a miraculous proof and a verse of revelation.
9.grammar: A singular noun. The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing pointed to or presented), or stands as the predicate of certain particles.

10.meaning: The daytime — the bright span of hours when the sun is up, from dawn to sunset; the natural counterpart of night.
10.grammar: A definite singular noun (the 'al-' prefix means 'the,' with its 'l' assimilated into the following 'n'). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the day') or as following a preposition or a particle that governs the genitive.
10.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — daylight, flowing/spreading open

11.meaning: An active adjective/participle meaning 'giving light / making things visible / sight-giving'. It describes something that illuminates so that things can be seen, or that is itself clearly visible and shedding light.
11.grammar: An active participle (form IV) on the muf'il pattern — 'one that causes seeing / sheds light'. The feminine -t plus the indefinite accusative -an (-tan) mark it as feminine and in the accusative case, typically describing a feminine object or completing a 'made it [to be] ___' statement.
11.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, seeing, perceiving

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'so that you (plural) may seek / pursue / strive after'. It denotes seeking out, desiring, and exerting effort to obtain something — such as seeking bounty or favor.
12.grammar: The prefix li- ('so that / in order to') marks purpose and puts the present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the final -na is dropped, leaving -ū for 'you (masculine plural)'. The form VIII pattern (with the infixed -t-) gives the sense of actively seeking for oneself.
12.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — seeking, desiring, striving after

13.meaning: Bounty, grace, favour, or abundance; something good given freely and beyond what is owed. It can mean material provision (such as profit from trade) or divine grace and excess generosity.
13.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -an (accusative case with nunation) typically marks it as the direct object of a verb ('seeking a bounty') or as the goal of an action. The nunation also makes it indefinite ('a bounty / some favour').
13.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be in excess, to surpass; hence grace, bounty, superiority

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

15.meaning: 'Your Lord' (addressing a group). 'Rabb' is a rich term: the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, possesses, provides for, and brings a thing to its proper completion — far more than a mere ruler.
15.grammar: A noun ('Lord') with an attached possessive pronoun, forming a possessive pairing. 'Rabb' carries a doubled (geminated) 'b' — the shaddah — at its core. The '-i' vowel on 'rabb' is its case ending, determined by 'Lord's' own role in the sentence (not by the suffix); the attached '-kum' is the possessor ('your'), addressing a plural 'you', and as the possessed-to term it sits in the genitive.
15.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'and so that you (plural) may know / come to know'. It denotes gaining knowledge, becoming aware of, or recognizing something.

parts.en: you know / come to know (present-tense verb)

16.grammar: Begins with 'and' (wa-), then li- ('so that / in order to') marking purpose, which puts the present-tense verb in the subjunctive mood; the final -na is therefore dropped, leaving -ū for 'you (masculine plural)' as the doers.

17.meaning: Number, count, or sum — the numerical total of a set of things. As the first word of a possessive phrase it gives 'the number OF ...'.
17.grammar: A singular noun. The '-a' ending marks the accusative case (here as object or complement). It is commonly the first term of a possessive pairing, followed by a noun in the genitive ('the number OF the years').

18.meaning: The years — successive twelve-month cycles; spans of time reckoned in years. Plural of 'sana' (a year).
18.grammar: A sound masculine-type plural ('years') made definite by 'al-' ('the'); its 'l' is assimilated into the following 's' (a 'sun letter'), hence the doubling. The '-īna' ending is the plural form used for the accusative/genitive — typically marking the word as an object or as linked to a preceding noun ('... OF the years').
18.root: س-ن-و / س-ن-ه (s-n-w / s-n-h) — year

19.meaning: 'and the reckoning/calculation' — the counting, computing, and working-out of amounts; by extension the calculation of time. The word carries the connective 'and'.
19.grammar: A singular noun made definite by 'al-' ('the') and joined by 'wa-' ('and'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative case (here object or complement); a word joined by 'and' normally takes the same case as what it is linked to.

20.meaning: And every / each / all: a word denoting comprehensiveness, applying a statement to each single member of a group or to the whole of something without exception.
20.grammar: A noun of totality, normally placed before another noun ('every …'). The -a ending is accusative, typically marking it as a direct object or a fronted object set before its verb. The prefix wa- means 'and'.

21.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
21.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
21.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

22.meaning: We expounded it / set it out in detail — a first-person plural past verb meaning to distinguish, detail, and explain something part by part, with an object pronoun referring to that thing.
22.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the intensive (form II) pattern, whose doubled middle consonant conveys doing the action thoroughly ('detailed out fully'). The suffix -nā marks the doer as 'we'; the final -hu is the masculine singular object pronoun, 'it / him.'

23.meaning: A noun meaning 'a making clear in detail / a thorough explaining / setting out distinctly'. It is a verbal noun for laying something out point by point so each part is distinct and fully explained.

parts.en: detailed explanation / setting out distinctly (verbal noun)

23.grammar: A verbal noun of the intensive form II (the doubled middle root letter conveys doing something thoroughly — separating into distinct parts). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the case typically used for the object of a verb or as an emphatic completion ('… explained it with [full] detail').
23.root: ف-ص-ل (f-ṣ-l) — separating, distinguishing, setting apart in detail

1.meaning: And every / each / all: a word denoting comprehensiveness, applying a statement to each single member of a group or to the whole of something without exception.
