9.grammar: A present-tense verb addressed to a single masculine 'you' (the ta- prefix). Its vowel-less ending (jussive mood) is the form used after particles like 'do not' (a command or prohibition) or 'if'; it does not stand as a plain statement on its own.
9.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, appoint, render

10.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
10.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: 'A god / a deity, an object of worship' — the word in its indefinite form, naming a single divine being without specifying which.
12.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending combines two things: the accusative case (the form for a verb's object or, often, a noun described by a following adjective) and nunation, the -n sound that signals 'a/an,' i.e. indefiniteness.
12.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

13.meaning: Another, other, a different one — a further item distinct from the one already mentioned.
13.grammar: An adjective/noun meaning 'other'. It belongs to a small group of words that resist the usual indefinite -n (nunation), so even when indefinite it takes a plain -a ending. That final -a is the accusative case, the form used for a direct object or one in agreement with such a noun.
13.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, come after, other

14.meaning: 'So you would be cast / thrown down' — a present-tense passive verb meaning that someone is hurled, flung, or cast, prefixed with a connector meaning 'so / then'.
14.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so / then', linking this to a preceding cause or condition. The verb is present-tense passive (the doer is unstated; the subject receives the action). The tu- prefix marks a second-person ('you') or feminine 'it' subject. The final -ā, with subjunctive force after fa-, signals a result or purpose ('so that you would be cast').
14.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to throw, cast, fling; to meet or encounter

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
15.root: — (particle)

16.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
16.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
16.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

17.meaning: Means 'blamed / blameworthy' — one who is reproached, censured, and held at fault. It describes a person open to criticism for their conduct.
17.grammar: A passive descriptive form ('one who is blamed'). The -an ending is accusative, the state for a descriptive complement or object. It portrays a person who has become a target of blame and reproach.

18.meaning: 'Driven away, banished, expelled' — a passive participle describing one who is repelled and cast out, pushed off and rejected.
18.grammar: A passive participle ('one who is driven off/expelled'), indefinite, with the -an ending (tanwīn) marking the accusative with indefiniteness. The accusative here is the descriptive 'state' case, characterizing someone as being in the condition of having been banished.
18.root: د-ح-ر (d-ḥ-r) — to drive away, repel, banish

1.meaning: 'So has He chosen / set apart for you?' — a question combining 'and/then' with 'has He selected exclusively', expressing astonishment or challenge at a supposed preference.
1.grammar: Opens with the interrogative a- ('has…? / is it that…?'), then the connector fa- ('then'). The core is a past-tense causative verb (form IV), third-person masculine 'he', meaning 'singled out / preferred'. The attached -kum is the plural object pronoun 'you (all)'. The combined opening conveys a rhetorical, often incredulous, question.
1.root: ص-ف-و (ṣ-f-w) — purity, clearness; to select the choicest, set apart

2.meaning: Your (plural) Lord — 'Rabb' means the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings a thing to its completion. It combines lordship with loving upbringing and care.
2.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The suffix '-kum' means 'your' (plural possessor). The '-u' on 'rabbu' before the suffix is the nominative case, marking the word as a subject or as a predicate standing on its own.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain, own

3.meaning: 'With / by sons' — the plural noun 'sons, male children', introduced by the preposition bi- ('with, by means of').
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with / by') is attached, followed by the article al-. 'Banīna' is a sound masculine plural ('sons'); its -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive case, which is the form such plurals take after a preposition. So the whole means 'with the sons'.
3.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — son, offspring; to build, beget

4.meaning: 'and he took / adopted (for himself)' — to take something up and make it one's own, e.g., to take as a friend, protector, or object of devotion; the reflexive (self-benefiting) form of 'to take.'
4.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he …'), in the reflexive (self-benefiting) stem 'to take for oneself / adopt.' The final -a marks a completed act done by 'he.' The leading 'wa-' means 'and'; the initial alif of the stem is a 'helping' vowel pronounced only when the word begins after a pause.

5.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
5.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

6.meaning: The angels — Allah's created beings of light who serve and obey Him and carry out His commands.
6.grammar: The definite plural noun 'angels' with the article al-. The word is a single broken (irregular) plural on the pattern mafāʿila, whose closing -a(t) belongs to the plural form itself and is not a separable suffix. The final '-i' is the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… of the angels').
6.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — an angel as a messenger/agent; possession, dominion

7.meaning: Females — daughters or female offspring; the plural of 'female', denoting members of the female sex.
7.grammar: A plural noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a predicate. 'Ināth' is a plural meaning 'females / daughters'.
7.root: أ-ن-ث ('-n-th) — femaleness; to be female, soft, or pliant

8.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
8.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.

9.meaning: 'You surely do say' — an emphatic present-tense verb of speaking, addressed to a group, stressing that they really do utter something.
9.grammar: The prefix la- adds emphasis ('surely, indeed'). The verb is present-tense; the ta-…-ūna frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The retained -na ending shows the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('you do say'), as opposed to a mood that would drop it.

10.meaning: 'A saying / word / statement' — an utterance or speech; that which is said.
10.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'a saying.' The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥ): it marks an indefinite noun in the accusative case, the form used for the object of a verb (e.g., 'to say a word') among other roles.
10.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say / speak / utter

11.meaning: 'Great, immense, tremendous' — describing something vast in magnitude or weight, whether in size, importance, or seriousness.
11.grammar: An adjective ('great, immense') in an intensive pattern. The -an ending (nunation with a final alif) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or for a description attached to such an object.
11.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, immense, mighty; greatness, a bone

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: We have turned about / set forth in various ways / explained from many angles — to repeatedly vary and diversify the presentation so a matter is made clear; the intensive Form II adds the sense of doing so again and again.
2.grammar: A Form II (intensive) past-tense verb with the suffix -nā ('we') marking the first-person plural past subject. Form II of this root conveys turning a matter this way and that, i.e. presenting it in varied, repeated forms; the whole means 'we have set [it] forth in diverse ways.'
2.root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to turn, divert; (Form II) to vary, diversify, expound repeatedly

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
4.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

5.meaning: The Qur'an — the recited Revelation; literally 'the Recitation/Reading,' the Book sent down to be recited aloud.
5.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'recitation/reading,' used as the proper name of the Book, with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive ending: it typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

6.meaning: 'So that they may take heed / be reminded' — a verb meaning to receive admonition, reflect, and bear something in mind, introduced by 'so that' expressing purpose.
6.grammar: The prefix li- means 'so that / in order that', expressing purpose. The verb is present-tense, third-person masculine plural ('they'), in an intensive reflexive pattern (form V). Its underlying shape is yatadhakkarū; the t of the prefix assimilates into the following dh (yatadhakkarū → yaddhakkarū), and in this spelling one dh is written, giving the sense 'to remind oneself, take heed'. After li- the verb is subjunctive: the plural ending appears as -ū (the final n dropped), marking purpose rather than a bare statement.
6.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind, take heed

7.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
7.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

8.meaning: 'It increases them / adds to them' — a present-tense verb meaning to make more, augment, or add, with an attached pronoun for those receiving the increase.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he / it'). The -u vowel before the pronoun is the indicative mood, signalling a plain ongoing or factual statement. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them', so the verb means 'it increases them / adds to them'.
8.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, grow, add, exceed

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: Aversion, flight, or shrinking away — a turning-away in revulsion or estrangement; recoiling from something.
10.grammar: A verbal noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). Here the accusative often serves as a 'specification' answering 'in what respect?' — e.g. increasing someone 'in aversion'. The noun names the action/state of fleeing or shrinking away.
10.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — to flee, shy away, recoil, be averse

1.meaning: An imperative command meaning 'Say!' or 'Speak!' — a direct order to one person to utter or declare something.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male. The bare, vowelless ending (the silent stop on the final 'l') marks it as a direct order: 'you, say!' It is built from the verb 'to say' with the weak middle letter dropped, leaving the short, clipped command form.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

2.meaning: If — a conditional particle introducing a hypothetical that is contrary to fact or unfulfilled ("if [such-and-such had been the case]…"), typically implying that because the condition did not hold, its result did not occur either.
2.grammar: A conditional particle. It has no ending to inflect. It sets up a supposed condition, classically one understood as unreal or unrealized, and is normally answered by a result clause (often introduced by la-, "surely [then]…").

3.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

3.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

4.meaning: Together with him; in his company or alongside him.
4.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment, 'with', joined to the attached pronoun -hu 'him'. Together they mean 'with him / in his company'.

5.meaning: Gods: beings or objects taken as deities and given worship. The plural of 'ilāh' (a god / object of worship), here in indefinite form.
5.grammar: A broken plural noun, indefinite. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) marks the nominative case with indefiniteness — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing being named or identified.

6.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
6.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

7.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
7.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

8.meaning: In that case / then — a response particle signaling that what follows is the consequence of a just-stated condition or supposition ('if so, then…').
8.grammar: A response/consequence particle, not a noun or verb. The -an ending is a fixed part of the word (written with a final alif), not a live grammatical case. It introduces the result side of a hypothetical ('then you would…').

9.meaning: 'They would surely have sought / striven for' — an emphatic past-tense verb meaning to seek out, pursue, or desire a way or means to something.

parts.en: surely (emphasis, in answer to a condition)

9.grammar: The prefix la- is the emphatic 'surely', the form used in the answer to a hypothetical 'if' clause. The verb is past-tense in an intensive 'seeking-for-oneself' pattern (form VIII). Its third-person masculine plural subject is carried by the final wāw, pronounced -aw ('they sought / strove'). The silent alif written after that wāw is only a spelling convention and is not pronounced.
9.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive after, aspire to

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
10.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

11.meaning: Possessor of / the one having — a relational word meaning 'owner of' or 'endowed with,' used to attach a quality or relationship to the noun it describes.
11.grammar: A relational noun meaning 'owner/possessor of,' which must be followed by another noun ('possessor OF …'). It declines for case: dhū (nominative), dhī (genitive), dhā (accusative). The form dhī (ending -ī) is its genitive, used when it follows a preposition or describes a preceding genitive noun. It never stands alone; it always governs a following noun.
11.root: — (a relational noun meaning 'possessor of'; no verbal root)

12.meaning: The Throne — the mighty seat of sovereignty and dominion. Literally a throne or canopy of a king; used as an image of supreme authority and rule.
12.grammar: A definite noun in the genitive case (the -i ending). The genitive appears when a noun follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun in a possessive 'X of Y' relationship. The l- prefix makes it definite ('the').
12.root: ع-ر-ش (ʿ-r-sh) — throne, canopy, seat of dominion

13.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
13.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

1.meaning: An exclamation of glorification meaning 'far removed and utterly above all imperfection is He.' The verbal noun 'subḥān' declares that the One referred to is exalted beyond any deficiency, partner, or fault, and the attached 'Him' directs that declaration to a single masculine being.
1.grammar: A verbal noun used as an absolute exclamation, fixed in the accusative ending -a (an emphatic declaration, roughly 'I declare His utter transcendence'). The attached -hu is the possessive/object pronoun 'Him', referring to one masculine person.
1.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide away, hence to declare Allah free of all imperfection

2.meaning: 'And He is exalted/transcendent high above' — to be far above and beyond, used of Allah being utterly lofty and removed from any deficiency or false attribution.
2.grammar: wa is 'and'. taʿālā is a past-tense verb (form VI) functioning as an exclamation of glorification; its final long -ā marks third-person masculine singular ('He'). The form intensifies the root sense to 'be supremely high, transcendent'.
2.root: ع-ل-و (ʿ-l-w) — to be high, lofty, exalted

3.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
3.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

4.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
4.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

5.meaning: Loftiness, exaltation — being high or elevated; when applied to conduct it means arrogance, overbearing pride, or tyrannical superiority.
5.grammar: A verbal noun (the abstract 'act/state' noun) of rising high. The final -an (with tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative ending, marking the word as an object or as an adverbial/specifying complement.

6.meaning: Large, great, big, or major — an adjective describing something of great size, amount, or importance. It can also mean elder/older in age. The -an ending leaves it indefinite ('a large …').
6.grammar: An indefinite adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn): it commonly marks the object of a verb, or works adverbially, and signals the word is indefinite ('a large one'). It pairs with ṣaghīr ('small').
6.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, largeness, being great or old

1.meaning: 'It glorifies / declares free of all imperfection' — a present-tense verb of extolling Allah's transcendence, proclaiming Him utterly above any flaw or likeness.
1.grammar: Present-tense verb in the intensive (form II) pattern, which conveys doing something fully or repeatedly. The tu- prefix marks a feminine third-person singular subject ('she / it'). The final -u is the indicative mood, marking a plain factual or ongoing statement. The verb means to extol Allah as far above every defect.
1.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide; to declare Allah free of all imperfection

2.meaning: To him / for him / he has — the preposition 'to/for' fused with a pronoun meaning 'him.' It expresses belonging, benefit, or possession (something is 'his' or done 'for him').
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-/la-' ('to, for') with the attached 3rd-person masculine singular pronoun 'him.' The pairing means 'to him' or 'for him' and often conveys possession ('he has …') or that an action is directed toward his benefit or detriment.
2.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the celestial expanse above, here in the plural ('the heavens'), encompassing all the layers of the sky. The definite article marks them as the known heavens.
3.grammar: A definite feminine sound plural ('the heavens'). The ending '-ātu' carries the -u that marks the nominative, generally signaling the subject or topic of the sentence ('the heavens [are …]').

4.meaning: 'The seven' — the cardinal number seven, made definite by 'the'; a count of seven things.
4.grammar: The number 'seven' made definite by the article al-, whose 'l' assimilates into the following 's' (a 'sun letter'), giving 'as-sabʿ'. The final -u is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject or topic of a sentence — the thing doing or being described.

5.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, and world beneath, as opposed to the heavens. The leading 'wa' joins it ('and …') and the definite article marks it as the known earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine noun joined by 'wa' ('and'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which generally marks the word as the subject or topic of a sentence ('and the earth [is …]').

6.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
6.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

7.meaning: A small unit: the preposition 'in / within / during' joined to the attached pronoun 'them' referring to a group of feminine things.
7.grammar: 'fī' is the preposition 'in/within/during'. The attached -hinna is the object pronoun 'them' for a group of feminine items, so the whole means 'in/among them'. Pronouns attached to a preposition like this always take the genitive form.

8.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
8.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

10.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
10.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
10.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

11.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
11.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: 'He / it glorifies, declares free of all imperfection' — a present-tense verb proclaiming Allah's absolute transcendence above every flaw.
12.grammar: Present-tense verb in the intensive (form II) pattern. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he / it'). The final -u is the indicative mood, signalling a plain, ongoing statement of fact. The verb means to extol Allah as utterly beyond any imperfection or likeness.
12.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide; to declare Allah free of all imperfection

13.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with His praise / praising Him' — accompanied by the acknowledgment of His perfect and praiseworthy attributes.
13.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with / by') is attached to the verbal noun ḥamd ('praise'), which carries the genitive -i ending because it follows a preposition. The attached -hi means 'His'; it appears as -hi (not -hu) because of the preceding -i vowel.
13.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — praise, commendation of what is good

14.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
14.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

15.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
15.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

16.meaning: 'You understand / comprehend deeply' — a present-tense verb of grasping a matter with insight and discernment, addressed to a group.
16.grammar: Present-tense verb; the ta-…-ūna frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The retained -na ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement of fact ('you do understand'). The root denotes a penetrating, discerning kind of comprehension — grasping the inner sense of a thing.
16.root: ف-ق-ه (f-q-h) — to understand deeply, comprehend, grasp with insight

17.meaning: 'Their glorification' — the verbal noun for declaring Allah free of all imperfection, joined to a possessive pronoun: the act of glorifying performed by them.
17.grammar: A verbal noun (form II, 'tasbīḥ') with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their'). The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative case, which commonly marks the object of a verb — the thing acted upon. So the word names the praise itself: 'their declaring of Allah's perfection'.
17.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide; to declare Allah free of all imperfection

18.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
18.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

19.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

19.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

20.meaning: Forbearing and clement — one who is gentle and patient, who does not rush to punish despite having full power to do so; a quality of dignified restraint.
20.grammar: An intensive adjective (the faʿīl pattern) describing a deep, settled quality, in the indefinite accusative marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative often marks a predicate after certain verbs or particles. The word denotes calm, patient restraint that withholds anger or punishment.

21.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
21.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: You recited / read out — the act of reading aloud or reciting, addressed to a single male. The base verb means to read, recite, or proclaim a text.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -ta marks the doer as 'you' (one male). Past-tense verbs report a completed action ('you read / you recited').

3.meaning: The Qur'an — the recited Scripture; literally 'the Recitation' or 'the Reading'.
3.grammar: A definite noun (carrying 'al-', 'the') on the verbal-noun pattern fuʿlān, denoting the act/thing of reciting. The final '-a' marks the accusative case, which most often signals that the word is the direct object of a verb.
3.root: ق-ر-ء (q-r-ʾ) — reciting, reading aloud, gathering words together

4.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
4.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

5.meaning: 'Between you' — the spatial/relational word 'between, amid', joined to a singular 'you', marking the position separating or linking two parties.
5.grammar: An adverb of place, 'bayna' ('between'), which always carries the accusative -a vowel as its fixed form. It is followed by the attached pronoun -ka, the second-person masculine singular 'you', so the whole means 'between you (and …)'.
5.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation and distinction; what lies between

6.meaning: 'And between'. A connective word meaning 'and between / and amid', used to mark the space, relationship, or distinction lying among two or more parties.
6.grammar: The word bayna ('between') with 'and' in front. It is an adverb of place that always leads into what follows, so it ends in a fixed -a and is normally paired with a following noun or pronoun ('between … and …').

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
9.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

10.meaning: The noun 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come,' linked by 'with / for / in exchange for' (bi-). The base word means 'the last, the latter, the final' (state of affairs) and is used as the standing name for the everlasting life after this world.
10.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the Hereafter') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('with / for / in exchange for'). The '-i' ending is genitive: the case a noun takes after a preposition (or when linked to a preceding noun as '…of…'). Here it appears because the preposition 'bi-' requires the genitive form; the tā' marbūṭa of the stem is sounded as 't' before this ending.
10.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

11.meaning: A barrier, screen, or veil — something that partitions, conceals, or blocks off, standing between two things.
11.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks the object of a verb — the thing acted upon (e.g. something placed or set). The noun names a partition that screens off or conceals.
11.root: ح-ج-ب (ḥ-j-b) — to veil, screen, block, conceal from view

12.meaning: Hidden, concealed, or veiled — covered over so as to be unseen; that which is screened from sight.
12.grammar: A passive participle ('that which is covered / concealed') on the pattern ma-...-ū-, naming the recipient of an action — here, the thing that is screened from view. It stands in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn), which commonly marks a descriptive word agreeing with a preceding accusative noun.
12.root: س-ت-ر (s-t-r) — to cover, veil, conceal, screen

1.meaning: 'And We made / We placed / We appointed.' A verb of making, fashioning, or setting something into a state or position, here joined to the preceding words by 'and.' Its sense ranges from creating and forming to assigning a role or rendering something a certain way.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with the attached subject ending -nā ('we'), marking a completed act done by a plural or majestic 'we.' The wa- prefix means 'and,' linking it to what precedes.
1.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

3.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
3.grammar: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
3.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

4.meaning: "Coverings, veils, wrappers." Things that envelop and conceal — sheaths or coverings placed over something so it cannot be reached or perceived.
4.grammar: A plural noun, indefinite ("coverings," not "the coverings"). The -an ending (tanwīn) marks both indefiniteness and the accusative case — the form a word takes when it is the object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

6.meaning: "That they should understand it / lest they grasp it." A present-tense verb meaning to comprehend deeply and grasp the inner sense of something, with an attached "it" as the thing understood.

parts.en: understand, comprehend deeply (the consonant cluster fq- carries no vowel of its own; the ya- prefix supplies the connecting vowel, so it sounds "-faqahū")

6.grammar: A present-tense verb, "they" (third-person masculine plural). Its underlying "-ūna" plural ending has dropped its final -na (becoming "-ū"), which signals the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form used after particles meaning "that," "so that," or "lest." The attached -hu is the object "it/him."
6.root: ف-ق-ه (f-q-h) — to understand, comprehend, gain insight

7.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
7.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

8.meaning: 'their ears' — the plural noun 'ears' joined to a possessive pronoun meaning 'their'.
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with an attached possessor. The -i vowel before the suffix is the genitive ending; here it arises because the noun is the first term (the possessed noun) in a possessive construct linked to its possessor, i.e. 'ears OF them'. The suffix appears as -him (rather than -hum) because it follows that -i sound. -him means 'their' for a group of males.
8.root: اذن (ʾ-dh-n) — ear; to listen / give ear

9.meaning: "Heaviness, a weight; deafness." Literally a heavy load or burden; used of the ears it means a heaviness that blocks hearing — i.e., deafness or hardness of hearing.
9.grammar: A singular noun, indefinite ("a heaviness"). The -an ending (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness together with the accusative case — the case a noun takes as the object of a verb or when otherwise governed into it.
9.root: و-ق-ر (w-q-r) — to be heavy, weighty; gravity, dignity

10.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
10.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

11.meaning: You mentioned, recalled, or called to mind; also to invoke, remember, or make remembrance of something or someone. The verb spans both speaking of a thing aloud and holding it present in the heart and memory.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -ta marks a completed action done by 'you' (one male person): 'you mentioned / you remembered.' The fixed -a vowel on this ending is the standard marker for a singular male addressee.
11.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

12.meaning: 'Your Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Owner, the One who nurtures and brings to completion) combined with 'your'. 'Rabb' carries the linked senses of ownership, authority, and ongoing care that raises a thing to its perfection.
12.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive. The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the word as a direct object or governed element. The attached -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
12.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing care, ownership and mastery

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: The Qur'an — the recited Revelation; literally 'the Recitation/Reading,' the Book sent down to be recited aloud.
14.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'recitation/reading,' used as the proper name of the Book, with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive ending: it typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
14.root: ق-ر-ا (q-r-ʾ) — to read, recite, gather/compile (words)

15.meaning: "Him alone / He being one and only" — a word expressing singularity and aloneness, with the pronoun "him" attached.
15.grammar: A fixed adverbial noun meaning "alone/only," used to stress singularity; it carries the accusative -a vowel as a circumstantial expression ("He, alone"). The suffix -hu refers back to a single male ("him").
15.root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d) — to be one, single, alone

16.meaning: They turned away, turned their backs, or went off in retreat; to wheel around and depart, often signalling rejection or withdrawal from something faced.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive (form II) pattern, which adds force to the bare sense of 'turning.' The plural -ū ending (here written -aw because the verb's last root letter is weak) marks the doers as 'they' — a group of males who completed the action.
16.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to turn, be near, take charge / turn away

17.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
17.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

18.meaning: Their backs — the rear or hinder parts of a body or thing; the plural of the word for 'back,' commonly used in the idiom of turning one's back in flight or aversion.
18.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun -him ('their,' for males). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically marks the word as the object of a preposition or as linked to a preceding word in an 'of' relationship.
18.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — back, hind part; to turn the back, to manage/ponder

19.meaning: Aversion, flight, or shrinking away — a turning-away in revulsion or estrangement; recoiling from something.
19.grammar: A verbal noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). Here the accusative often serves as a 'specification' answering 'in what respect?' — e.g. increasing someone 'in aversion'. The noun names the action/state of fleeing or shrinking away.
19.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — to flee, shy away, recoil, be averse

1.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
1.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

2.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
2.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
3.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

4.meaning: They listen, give ear, or pay attention; this verb pattern conveys actively and deliberately listening to something, lending one's ear rather than merely hearing in passing.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb in a reflexive/middle-voice (form VIII) pattern, which here adds the sense of taking in a sound for oneself — listening attentively rather than merely hearing. The prefix ya- marks a third-person ('he/they') subject, and the ending -ūna marks a male plural subject in an ongoing or habitual action: 'they listen / are listening.'

5.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

7.meaning: They listen, give ear, or pay attention; this verb pattern conveys actively and deliberately listening to something, lending one's ear rather than merely hearing in passing.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb in a reflexive/middle-voice (form VIII) pattern, which here adds the sense of taking in a sound for oneself — listening attentively rather than merely hearing. The prefix ya- marks a third-person ('he/they') subject, and the ending -ūna marks a male plural subject in an ongoing or habitual action: 'they listen / are listening.'

8.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
8.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

9.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
9.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

10.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
10.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

11.meaning: A secret talk, private conversation, or confidential whispering exchanged between people apart from others; the act or content of conferring in hushed, hidden speech.
11.grammar: A noun (a verbal noun naming the act of secret conferring). It ends in a fixed long -ā (written as a 'broken' alif), an ending that does not change for case, so the word keeps one form whether subject, object, or possessive.
11.root: ن-ج-و (n-j-w) — to confide secretly, save/deliver; private talk

12.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
12.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

13.meaning: 'He says' or 'he is saying' — the act of speaking or uttering words. The imperfect tense conveys an ongoing, habitual, or present/future action.
13.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he', the stem qūl carries the meaning 'say', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement (as opposed to a subjunctive -a or jussive sukūn used after certain particles).

14.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who do wrong, act unjustly, or place things where they do not belong. The underlying image is one who oppresses, transgresses limits, and deals unjustly with others or with themselves.
14.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word functions as the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence.
14.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression

15.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
15.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

16.meaning: You follow, pursue, or adhere to something; you take it as a path or guide and walk behind it. It implies following step by step, whether a person, teaching, or mere assumption.
16.grammar: A present-tense Form VIII verb. The '-ūna' ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all') and indicative mood, presenting the following as an ongoing or habitual action.

17.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
17.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

18.meaning: 'A man' — an adult male human being. The word denotes a man specifically as a male individual, often with a sense of full-grown manhood.
18.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks the indefinite accusative, typically the case of a direct object or of a predicate following certain particles.
18.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — manhood, the adult male; (also the foot/to go on foot)

19.meaning: One who has been bewitched, enchanted, or affected by sorcery; a person whose mind or senses are described as overcome by magic.
19.grammar: A passive participle (the 'done-to' form: 'one who is bewitched'). The ending -an marks the accusative case on an indefinite noun — typically the object of a verb or a predicate naming what someone is said to be ('… a bewitched one').

1.meaning: A command 'look! / consider! / observe!' It directs the listener to turn their gaze or attention toward something, whether with the eye or with the mind.
1.grammar: A singular masculine imperative (command) addressed to 'you'. The helping 'u' at the start lets the cluster be pronounced, and the vowelless final consonant (-ur with sukūn) is the standard imperative ending, issuing a direct order.
1.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, to see, to consider

2.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
2.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

3.meaning: They struck out / set forth / journeyed through the land. From a root meaning 'to strike,' it idiomatically means to travel or venture out, often for trade or a campaign.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form I verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (did).' The written final alif after the wāw is silent (a spelling convention for plural verb endings).
3.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike; by extension, to travel/set forth

4.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
4.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.

5.meaning: The likenesses / parables / examples — the plural of mathal, a comparison, similitude, or illustrative example used to make a truth vivid. The al- prefix makes it definite ('the examples').
5.grammar: A definite plural noun (with al-). The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

6.meaning: So they strayed, went astray, lost their way, or erred; to wander off the right path, whether literally losing one's road or figuratively falling into error and misguidance.
6.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then,' linking this to what precedes as a result or sequel. The verb is past tense, and the plural -ū ending marks the doers as 'they' (a group of males) who completed the action: 'so they strayed.'
6.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, err, be lost

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
7.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

8.meaning: They are able / they have the power and capacity — to be capable of doing something, to have the strength, means, or ability to carry it out.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the present tense and the 'they' subject; the -ūna ending marks the plural and the indicative mood — the plain factual form for an ongoing state. From form X, which often carries the sense of 'seeking/having the capacity for' something, here simply 'to be able.'
8.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, to be capable, willing capacity

9.meaning: A way, path, road, or means — a route to a destination, hence also a way or means of accomplishing something.
9.grammar: A singular noun. The '-an' ending is accusative and indefinite: the accusative case commonly marks the direct object of a verb, and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite ('a way'). It denotes a path one travels or a means to an end.

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'is it when…?' — an interrogative 'is it / really?' joined to 'when', used to question or express astonishment about a future circumstance or event.
2.grammar: Two particles fused together. The opening hamza a- is the question marker that turns a statement into a yes/no question (often carrying a tone of incredulity). 'idhā' is a particle meaning 'when / at the time that', normally pointing to something expected to occur. Particles do not take case endings.

3.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
3.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

4.meaning: Bones — the hard skeletal pieces of a body; the plural of the word for 'bone.' The same root carries the idea of being great, mighty, or weighty.
4.grammar: A plural noun. The ending -an marks the accusative case on an indefinite noun, which typically signals it is the object of a verb ('… bones') or otherwise governed within the sentence.
4.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — bone; to be great, mighty, immense

5.meaning: And crumbled fragments, dust, or decayed particles; the disintegrated remains of something broken down into tiny crumbled pieces.
5.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and,' joining this word to a preceding item. The noun ends in -an, the accusative case on an indefinite noun, typically marking it as a verb's object or as parallel to another accusative word it is joined with.
5.root: ر-ف-ت (r-f-t) — to crumble, break into fragments; dust, debris

6.meaning: 'is it that we…?' — an incredulous question 'really, will we…?' built on the emphatic particle 'inna with an attached 'we'.

parts.en: indeed / it is the case that

6.grammar: A questioning hamza a- prefixed to 'inna, an emphasis particle that strongly affirms a statement ('truly / indeed it is so'). Together the sense is a disbelieving 'is it really the case that…?'. The attached -nā is the first-person-plural suffix pronoun 'we' (the subject being emphasized). 'inna grammatically governs a following noun in the accusative case.

7.meaning: Surely going to be raised up; certainly to be resurrected and brought back to life. The passive participle names those upon whom the raising is done, and the prefixed 'truly' adds strong emphasis.
7.grammar: An emphatic particle la- ('surely') on a passive participle (maf'ūl pattern), masculine sound plural. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject/predicate) case; the participle means 'ones who are raised,' and la- stresses the certainty.
7.root: ب-ع-ث (b-ʿ-th) — to send, raise up, resurrect

8.meaning: A creation, a created thing, or the act/manner of creating; what is brought into being. The root also gives the sense of moulding, fashioning, and even innate disposition or character.
8.grammar: A verbal noun. The ending -an marks the accusative case on an indefinite noun, which here typically functions as an object or as a noun specifying the manner or result of an action ('… as a creation').

9.meaning: New, fresh, recently made or renewed; something brought newly into being, the opposite of old or worn.
9.grammar: An adjective in the common fa'īl pattern. The ending -an marks the indefinite accusative case; an adjective in this case typically agrees with and describes an accusative noun ('a new …').
9.root: ج-د-د (j-d-d) — to be new, renew; newness, seriousness

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: Be! Become! A command to exist as, or to enter into, whatever is then described.
2.grammar: An imperative (command) verb from the verb 'to be / to become', addressed to a group. The long -ū ending (و followed by a silent alif) marks the command as directed at 'you all' (masculine plural). As a command it carries no case ending of its own.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to become, to come into existence

3.meaning: Stones; pieces of rock. This is the broken (irregular) plural of the singular noun ḥajar ('a stone'), denoting stones in the plural.
3.grammar: A feminine broken plural of ḥajar ('stone'), ending in tāʾ marbūṭa. It carries tanwīn fatḥa (the -an ending), the accusative case with 'nunation,' marking an indefinite noun ('stones / some stones') that typically functions as a direct object or specifier of quantity.

4.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
4.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

5.meaning: Iron — the hard metal; the substance itself. By extension the root conveys sharpness, hardness, and keenness.
5.grammar: A noun (also usable as an adjective meaning 'sharp'). The ending -an marks the indefinite accusative case, which typically signals the word is a verb's object or a predicate naming what something is made to be ('… iron').
5.root: ح-د-د (ḥ-d-d) — iron; to be sharp, to delimit

1.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
1.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

2.meaning: A creation, a created thing, or the act/manner of creating; what is brought into being. The root also gives the sense of moulding, fashioning, and even innate disposition or character.
2.grammar: A verbal noun. The ending -an marks the accusative case on an indefinite noun, which here typically functions as an object or as a noun specifying the manner or result of an action ('… as a creation').

3.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
3.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

4.meaning: It grows great, becomes large, or looms big; to increase in size, magnitude, or seriousness. The verb can describe something physically expanding or a matter weighing heavily in the mind.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb. The prefix ya- marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he' or 'it'), and the final -u vowel marks the plain (indicative) present, used for an ongoing or general action: 'it grows great / is great.'
4.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, big, grow large

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: Your chests/breasts — the bosoms, figuratively the seat of one's inner thoughts, intentions, and feelings (plural of ṣadr, 'chest').
6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'ṣadr.' The '-i' is the genitive case, here required because the noun carries a possessive pronoun: the attached '-kum' means 'your (all)' and grammatically possesses the noun ('the chests OF you').

7.meaning: Then they will say — a verb of speaking set in the future, declaring that a group will speak; 'then/so they are going to say.'
7.grammar: Layered prefixes: fa- ('then'), sa- ('will,' marking the future). The verb is present-tense with ya-…-ūna for 'they' (plural masculine). The full -ūna ending is the indicative form, used for a plain statement (not a command or negated form).

8.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
8.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

9.meaning: He restores us, brings us back, or returns us; to cause to come back again or repeat. The causative pattern means making something return to a former state.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb in a causative (form IV) pattern, meaning 'to bring back / make return.' The prefix yu- marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'), and the attached -nā is the object 'us': 'he brings us back.' The verb's indicative -u vowel sits before the pronoun.
9.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — to return, come back, repeat

10.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.
10.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak

11.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

12.meaning: He originated you, brought you into being, or fashioned you from nothing; to bring forth a thing fresh and unprecedented. The root carries the sense of splitting open into existence and of innate, original nature.
12.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then,' linking this as a sequel or consequence. The verb is past tense (a completed act by 'he'), and the attached -kum is the object 'you' (a group, addressed as males): 'so He originated you.'
12.root: ف-ط-ر (f-ṭ-r) — to originate, bring into being, cleave; innate nature

13.meaning: First, foremost — the one that comes before all others in time, order, or rank.
13.grammar: A noun/adjective meaning 'first', here in a form that does not take normal indefinite case-tanwīn (a 'diptote'). The -a ending is accusative, marking it as an object or, very often, as the leading term of a possessive phrase ('the first of …').
13.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to return to a beginning

14.meaning: One time / once / an instance — a noun denoting a single occurrence of an act. Indefinite ('a time'), as shown by its two-vowel (tanwin) ending.
14.grammar: A feminine noun meaning 'a single time/occurrence'. The doubled-vowel ending (tanwin, here -in) marks it as indefinite ('a time', not 'the time'); the -i quality of that ending is genitive, signalling the word follows a preposition or links to another noun. It often expresses 'one time / once'.
14.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — passing by; an instance or occurrence of something

15.meaning: Then they will shake or wag (their heads) at someone; to toss or move the head in a gesture commonly expressing scorn, mockery, or dismissal.
15.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then,' and sa- marks the near future ('will'). The verb is in a causative (form IV) present tense: the prefix yu- marks a third-person subject and the -ūna ending marks a male plural ('they'), giving 'then they will shake.'
15.root: ن-غ-ض (n-gh-ḍ) — to shake, toss (the head), move to and fro

16.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
16.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

17.meaning: Their heads — the uppermost part of the body; the plural of the word for 'head,' here belonging to a group.
17.grammar: A plural noun with the attached possessive pronoun -hum ('their,' for males). The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb ('… their heads').

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they say / and they keep saying' — to utter or assert in speech. The structure presents an ongoing or repeated act of speaking by a group.
18.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb joined by wa- ('and'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks the 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'); the full -ūna ending is the inseparable indicative-plural suffix, showing the verb is in its base (indicative) form and expressing an ongoing or habitual action.
18.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

19.meaning: When? — an interrogative asking about the time of something.
19.grammar: An indeclinable question word meaning 'when?'; it asks about the time of an event and does not change its ending.

20.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
20.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

21.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
21.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

22.meaning: It may be that / perhaps — a verb of approximation expressing hopeful expectation or near-likelihood that something will come about. When used of Allah it conveys an outcome that is sure to be realized rather than mere doubt.
22.grammar: A verb of approximation (one of the 'verbs of hoping/nearness'), defective and non-conjugating: it stays fixed in this form and does not change for tense or person. Its final -ā reflects the underlying weak root letter. It introduces an expected or hoped-for possibility, typically followed by a clause stating what may occur.
22.root: ع-س-و / ع-س-ي (ʿ-s-w/y) — to be hoped for, to be near (verb of approximation/hope)

23.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
23.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

24.meaning: '(That) He be / there be' — a form of the core verb 'to be/become', expressing existence or a state of being.
24.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he is/becomes' or 'there is'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after certain particles (e.g. 'that', 'so that', 'in order to') and giving the sense of a dependent or hoped-for action.
24.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

25.meaning: An adjective meaning 'near, close, close at hand' — describing something short in distance, time, or relationship, easily reached or soon to come.
25.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern ('near, close'). The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (nunation), which typically marks the word as agreeing with an accusative noun it describes, or otherwise governed into the accusative; the tanwīn shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

2.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he calls / summons / invites you (plural)' — to call out to someone, beckoning or summoning them.
2.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The ya- prefix marks 'he'; the verb ends in the weak long vowel -ū of its root. The attached -kum is the direct object 'you all'.
2.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, supplicate

3.meaning: And you respond, answer, or comply with a call; this verb pattern conveys answering favourably and obeying a summons or request.
3.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'and so' or 'then.' The verb is a present-tense form X (a 'seeking/responding' pattern). The prefix ta- here marks a second-person plural subject ('you all'), and the -ūna ending confirms a male plural in an ongoing/future action: 'and you respond.'

4.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with His praise / praising Him' — accompanied by the acknowledgment of His perfect and praiseworthy attributes.
4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with / by') is attached to the verbal noun ḥamd ('praise'), which carries the genitive -i ending because it follows a preposition. The attached -hi means 'His'; it appears as -hi (not -hu) because of the preceding -i vowel.
4.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — praise, commendation of what is good

5.meaning: And you suppose, think, reckon, or presume; to hold an opinion or conjecture. The root spans from uncertain guessing to firm assumption, depending on context.
5.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and.' The verb is present tense; the prefix ta- marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks a male plural in an ongoing or future action: 'and you suppose / will think.'
